The Tool Decathlon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Diverse, Realistic, and Long-Horizon Task Execution
The Tool Decathlon (dubbed as Toolathlon) is a benchmark for language agents offering diverse applications and tools, realistic environment setup, and reliable execution-based evaluation.
Toolathlon spans 32 software applications and 604 tools, ranging from everyday platforms such as Google Calendar and Notion to professional applications like WooCommerce, Kubernetes, and BigQuery.
And it includes 108 manually sourced or crafted tasks in total, requiring interacting with multiple applications over approximately 20 interaction turns on average to complete.
Each task is strictly verifiable through dedicated evaluation scripts.
Released June 30, 2026

Toolathlon-Verified is the current release of the benchmark. It includes substantial revisions to many tasks and the supporting infrastructure to ensure task correctness and reliable evaluation. These changes have been validated through extensive experiments.

Toolathlon-Verified is not a new, smaller subset. Both versions contain the same 108 tasks, with no task added, removed, or renamed.

It preserves the original 108-task scope while revising the task definitions, initial states, ground truth, evaluators, and execution infrastructure that turn those tasks into a trustworthy benchmark.

A benchmark failure should point to agent capability—not ambiguous instructions, stale data, brittle formatting checks, leaked state, or an external service that has not propagated yet.
External-service failures are not agent failures Toolathlon tasks use real services, so a successful write and an immediately visible read are not always the same event.
Finally, we evaluated each of the eight reported models across three benchmark runs.
Evaluation visibility: 43 task evaluators now use shared or equivalent bounded whole-check retries for cases where a service accepted a write but has not exposed it to the grader yet.
The evaluator uses trusted configuration and host-observed execution state rather than trusting fields that an agent could write into its own trajectory.
The default phased containerized and decoupled runners both apply this protection.
At the model boundary, Toolathlon normalizes model-visible tool names and handles provider differences in reasoning and tool-call payloads.
